review.tagline: Policy-enforced sandbox runtime for autonomous AI agents
review.summary: OpenShell runs each agent in an isolated sandbox where kernel controls restrict file access and system calls, and every outbound network connection is checked against a declared policy. Real credentials are injected only into requests bound for approved endpoints, and policy changes are checked with formal verification so risky new access waits for human review. It ships a CLI and gateway, SDKs for four languages, and a Helm chart.
review.audience: Teams running autonomous agents that need enforced access limits
strengths: Filesystem, syscall and network rules declared per agent in a policy
Agents never see real credentials; injected only for approved endpoints
Policy changes are formally verified and gated for human review
SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Go and Rust; Helm chart for Kubernetes
weaknesses: Default sandbox image is minimal Ubuntu with no agent installed
Windows support is via WSL 2 and marked experimental
Kubernetes needs a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy
Anonymous telemetry is on by default; opt-out required
needs: Needs Docker, Podman or host virtualization, Kubernetes with NetworkPolicy-enforcing CNI (optional)
